leader.directive:
METHOD TURN: the user asked for a pre-mortem. This reply follows the method below exactly, and calls no tools.
The plan to stress-test is ‘Raise prices 10%’. The goal is ‘monthly recurring revenue’.
Shape: 2 failure stories (at most 3) told in the past tense ('Imagine ‘Raise prices 10%’ went badly because…'). Each story: one or two sentences, rests on at least one supplied item, then 'Watch for:' one early warning sign and 'Mitigate:' one action. Then ONE line 'Outside the model: …?': a blind spot the model does not capture (DSK-P-001 step 2), asked as a question, never asserted, never numbered.
The model holds no horizon for the goal: set no date or period of your own.
Format: Insight line, then 2-3 stories as a numbered list (each contains 'Watch for:' and 'Mitigate:'), then one 'Outside the model: …?' line.
Each story rests on at least one of these items from the user’s model, highest priority first. Name the item in its own words; for a link, name both ends:
- ‘Price-rise customer losses’ (a risk on this plan’s path)
Name no option other than ‘Raise prices 10%’. Outside an item's own name, use no percentage and none of these words: likely, likelihood, chance, probability, probable, odds. Never say anything will fail: tell each story in the past tense.
Never: a probability, percentage or win share unless the user stated it.
Never: a leading option when run.leader_licensed is false.
Never: 'the model was saved', implementation detail, internal ids.
Never: EVPI, elasticity, sensitivity score, placeholder, edge, node.
At most 180 words.
